summary: Read-only adversarial correctness bug-hunt across the 3 fused megakernels + wgmma substrate + grid-barrier/determinism + the 33-cell dispatch + optimizer tails; each candidate bug refuted-by-default before confirmation
logs: Hunt found 11 candidate bugs across 7 areas; refuting each (2 skeptics, refute-by-default).
2/11 candidate bugs CONFIRMED by adversarial verification.

confirmed.area: optimizer tail — SuperGrok11 cosine gate (L3-TC staged precompute, all 3 models)
confirmed.description: CONFIRMED. The L3-TC staged SG11 per-tensor gate computes cos(grad, MU) (the meta-net output) instead of the algorithm's cos(grad, MOMENTUM) (Adam exp_avg). The reduction loop reads sg=grad[gi], u=mu_blob[gi], then accumulates num+=sg*u, den_g+=sg*sg, den_m+=u*u — i.e. cos(grad,mu) — then sg11_finalize_gate(num,den_g,den_m,gate_temp). The helper has NO momentum parameter at all. This contradicts the single source of truth in three places: (1) canonical csrc/algorithms/supergrok11.h:24-30,64 and the un-inlined sweep-A sg11_sweep_a_step (lines 86-105) accumulate gate_num+=g*momentum, gate_den_m+=momentum*momentum; (2) the live per-op kernel sg11_sweep_a_kernel takes a dedicated `momentum` pointer and reduces over it (verified in worktree grokking_optimizers/kernels/sm_90/supergrok11_sm90.cuh:82-101); (3) the Python source of truth supergrok11.py:4-11,91 and SharpnessMetaNet docstring state gate=sigmoid(gate_temperature*cos_sim(grad,momentum)). Because the staged path re-inlines the reduction (rather than calling the canonical sg11_sweep_a_step) the wrong operand slipped past the drift guard. All three SG11 cells (decoder/vit/mamba) inherit the same wrong operand at the call sites listed.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Reduce the gate against the Adam momentum buffer (exp_avg), not mu. (1) Add `const float* __restrict__ momentum` to sg11_precompute_mu_and_gate_for_tensor; keep the mu write loop (526-532) unchanged (mu is still needed for smart_grad), but in the gate loop (540-547) use mom=momentum[gi] so num+=sg*mom; den_g+=sg*sg; den_m+=mom*mom. Read momentum BEFORE the apply tail writes it — ordering is safe because the precompute runs first (decoder:1452-1456) and the apply (opt_components.cuh:503, sg11_sweep_b_step which writes exp_avg[idx]) runs after, so the precompute captures start-of-step momentum exactly as canonical sweep-A does. (2) At the 3 call sites pass st.exp_avg (the same base apply rebases to ts.exp_avg=st.exp_avg+off), so momentum indexes [off+i] consistently with grad/mu. st.exp_avg is a confirmed live field in FusedOptState (opt_components.cuh:107) read by the apply. (3) Preferably route the reduction through canonical algo::sg11_sweep_a_step so the body is single-sourced and drift-guarded (this also fuses the mu write, since sg11_sweep_a_step writes mu_out[idx]). (4) Fix the now-wrong oracles/comments so the gate catches this going forward: tests/hw/test_opt_stages.py _sg11_gate_oracle_fp64/_sg11_gate_mirror_fp32 (lines 201-226) and tests/hw/test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:777-778 currently compute cos(grad,mu) — re-point them at the exp_avg (start-of-step momentum) slice; update the cos(grad,mu) comments in opt_stages_precompute.cuh:446,472-480,509-510,537-538 and opt_components.cuh:199. CAVEAT for the ratchet: re-run the fp64 parity + A/A/A gate with the CORRECTED reference AND a warm-up step so exp_avg!=0 — at step 1 rescale=0 (mu≈0) AND momentum=0, so den_m≈0→cos=0→gate=0.5 in BOTH formulations; the step-1 coincidence will keep even a corrected oracle green and blind to the change.

confirmed.area: optimizer tail — SuperGrok11 staged reduction not bound to canonical single source (drift-guard gap; secondary to SG11-GATE-COS-OPERAND)
confirmed.description: CONFIRMED as the maintainability root-cause of SG11-GATE-COS-OPERAND, not an independent numeric bug. The header contract (opt_stages_precompute.cuh:26-28) says elementwise math must CALL the canonical fn, never re-inline. The staged helper DOES call canonical sg11_phi_forward (530) and sg11_finalize_gate (558), but it open-codes the cosine reduction body (539-547) instead of calling canonical sg11_sweep_a_step (supergrok11.h:86-105). There is no compiled call site binding the staged reduction to the canonical reduction, and check_math_single_source.py does not scan opt_stages_precompute.cuh for a cosine-reduction re-inline pattern — which is exactly how the wrong operand (mu vs momentum) drifted in undetected. This entry exists so the fix doesn't merely patch the operand but also closes the hole; left open, a future edit to canonical sg11_sweep_a_step would again silently fail to propagate to the L3-TC path.
confirmed.fix_sketch: Fold into the SG11-GATE-COS-OPERAND fix: route the staged Sweep-A reduction through algo::sg11_sweep_a_step (which reduces over momentum and writes mu in one pass), eliminating the re-inlined body. Then harden the guard: add opt_stages_precompute.cuh to check_math_single_source.py's consumer-header scan and add a cosine-reduction re-inline pattern (e.g. flag `den_m += <expr>*<expr>` accumulators outside a canonical call) so any future staged re-inline of the cosine is rejected at self-test time. No separate numeric change beyond what SG11-GATE-COS-OPERAND already requires.

triage.notes:
VERDICT: the two CONFIRMED candidates (SG11-GATE-COS-OPERAND and SG11-STAGED-IGNORES-CANONICAL-DRIFT) are ONE underlying defect — the staged SG11 gate uses the wrong cosine second operand (mu instead of momentum) — with the re-inlined reduction being the maintainability mechanism that let it drift. Merged into: a major bug (the operand) + a minor sub-item (the drift-guard gap) whose fix should be applied together. I did NOT split them into independent items because the minor one has no standalone numeric effect.

LIVE-CODE VERIFICATION (all against the main tree, not docs):
- Wrong operand confirmed at opt_stages_precompute.cuh:542-546 (reads mu_blob, accumulates u*u for den_m).
- All 3 call sites confirmed to pass (st.mu, grad, st.sharpness) with NO momentum: decoder 1452-1454, vit 1090-1092, mamba 1159-1161 — identical port across all three SG11 cells.
- Canonical truth confirmed: supergrok11.h:24-30,64 (gate_num+=grad*momentum), sg11_sweep_a_step:101-104 reads a `momentum` pointer; per-op sg11_sweep_a_kernel:82-101 passes a dedicated momentum tensor; Python supergrok11.py:4-11,91 documents cos_sim(grad,momentum).
- Fix feasibility confirmed: st.exp_avg is a real field (opt_components.cuh:107) read by the SG11 apply at opt_components.cuh:503; the apply's sg11_sweep_b_step writes exp_avg[idx] (supergrok11.h:134). Precompute runs BEFORE apply in the same per-tensor body, so reading st.exp_avg in the precompute correctly captures start-of-step momentum — matching the canonical sweep-A/sweep-B ordering. No grid barrier needed (per-tensor, single CTA).

WHY THE GATE MISSES IT (scale flag — keep but understand): both the fp64 oracle (test_opt_stages.py:217-226) and the tail-gate ref (test_l3tc_tail_gate.py:777-778) were written to compute cos(grad,mu) — they mirror the kernel, not the algorithm, so they are co-wrong and never flag the divergence. Additionally, at step 1 the SharpnessMetaNet rescale=0 (supergrok11.py:58) makes mu≈0 AND exp_avg=0, so den_m≈0 → cos=0 → gate=sigmoid(0)=0.5 in BOTH formulations. The two formulations COINCIDE early; divergence only appears once the meta-net trains rescale!=0 and momentum accumulates (many steps in / at scale). So single-step fp64 parity + A/A/A bit-determinism stay green while the multi-step trajectory of all three SG11 cells silently diverges from the documented algorithm. This is a gate-blind, scale/multi-step bug — exactly the class requested.

PARITY/RATCHET CAUTION: the operand fix CHANGES numerics (parity_safe=false for SG11-GATE-COS-OPERAND), so it must go through the fp64-gated ratchet with the CORRECTED reference (cos(grad,momentum)) and a forced-nonzero exp_avg (warm-up step); otherwise the step-1 momentum=0 coincidence keeps the test blind even after the fix. The drift-guard hardening itself (SG11-STAGED-DRIFT-GUARD) is transport-only / parity_safe=true once the operand is correct. NOTE: before merging system-wide, the OWNER should confirm cos(grad,momentum) is the intended algorithm — every authoritative source (canonical header, per-op kernel, Python, gfx942/Pallas references per the candidate evidence) says momentum; only the SM90 staged path and its co-wrong oracle say mu. If the owner instead declares mu canonical, the fix is documentation-only (reconcile the contradicting prose) — but that would require flipping the canonical header + per-op kernel + Python to mu, which contradicts the per-op `momentum` plumbing that already ships. The weight of evidence is that momentum is correct and the staged path is the outlier.

I did not find any additional confirmed bugs in scope beyond these two during verification; this list reflects only the adversarially-confirmed input, validated against live code.
